newsitem.title: USA: Micrion adopts shareholder rights plan.
newsitem.headline: Micrion adopts shareholder rights plan.

text.p: Micrion Corp said Wednesday it has adopted a shareholder rights plan that would be triggered if any group or individual acquired at least 15 percent of its stock.
Under the plan, the company has declared a dividend of one preferred share purchase right for each share of Micrion's common stock outstanding as of the close of business on August 4.
Each right will entitle shareholders to purchase from Micrion one one-thousandth of a share of Series A Junior Preferred Stock at an exercise price of $90.
Micrion said the adoption of the rights plan was not a response "to any takeover offer, either real or anticipated."

Initially, the rights will trade together with Micrion's common stock and will not be exercisable. The rights will become exercisable following the 10th business day after the announcement that a person or group has acquired 15 percent or more of Micrion's common stock, or following the 10th business day after the announcement of a tender or exchange offer.
The rights expire July 30, 2007, unless redeemed earlier by Micrion's board of directors.

If the rights become exercisable, each right not owned by a person or group holding 15 percent or more of Micrion's common stock will entitle its owner to purchase, at the right's then-current exercise price, that number of shares of Micrion common stock having a market value at that time equal to twice the right's then-current exercise price.
